subject: Island deployment artifact signing & acceptance — schedule + checklist
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: ops-eng@northstar-dc.com
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Island deployment artifact signing & acceptance — proposed window

Hi team,

We’re preparing the sealed artifact bundle for the NorthStar island deployment and want to lock down the acceptance flow and sign-off window so the courier and site operator have a single playbook. High-level plan below:

- Redwood produces release bundle (island_manifest_v1.2.tar).
- Bundle signed with Redwood HSM-backed signing key (detached .sig).
- Courier delivers sealed media and printed manifest; site operator verifies signature and completes a site acceptance form.
- Operator turns machine on in the airlock; operator confirms checks from acceptance checklist; Redwood receives signed acceptance form.

Questions for your ops team:
1) Confirm courier ETA range (two-day window) and preferred delivery time (morning vs afternoon).
2) Provide the local operator point-of-contact and their preferred way to transmit the signed acceptance (email scanned PDF vs secure upload).
3) Are you able to validate SHA256 fingerprints on-site or do you want us to provide a QR-coded manifest?

Attachments: draft chain_of_custody_template.xlsx (template for operator to sign).

Goal: schedule the delivery for week of Sep 22 and lock acceptance steps by Sep 17 so we can sign the manifest and hand it to the courier on Sep 21.

If that window works, I’ll produce the signed manifest and include a short operator checklist.

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Carla Vega <carla.vega@aegis-svcs.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-eng@northstar-dc.com, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 11:18:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Island deployment artifact signing & acceptance — proposed window

Karthik —

Thanks for the summary. NorthStar ops confirms the week of Sep 22 is acceptable. Courier (Aegis Logistics) can do a morning delivery window (08:00–11:00 local). Our on-site acceptance lead is Diego Ramos (diego.ramos@northstar-dc.com). He prefers secure upload to our SFTP (ops-eng@northstar-dc.com will provide creds in a separate message) but can also scan and email if SFTP is unavailable.

We can validate SHA256 fingerprints on-site but would appreciate a printed QR on the manifest as a secondary verification. Two operational notes:

- We do accept detached signatures but need the signer identity assertion (certificate chain) and a short statement of key custody (where the Redwood signing key is held and whether it is HSM-protected).
- Please confirm whether Redwood expects site operators to sign the chain_of_custody_template.xlsx or whether Aegis Logistics should sign first at pickup.

I’ll loop Diego on a follow-up once you send the signed manifest.

—Carla
Carla Vega
Sr. Integrations Manager, Aegis Systems (logistics partner)
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Carla Vega <carla.vega@aegis-svcs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Island deployment artifact signing & acceptance — proposed window

Carla / Diego (when you’re in the thread) —

Quick clarifications from Redwood security and ops:

- Signing: Redwood will produce a detached signature (island_manifest_v1.2.tar.sig) created inside our FIPS-validated HSM. We will include the signer certificate and the signing statement (one-page) describing key custody and signing timestamp.
- Chain-of-custody: Aegis Logistics should sign the pickup portion at courier dispatch; site operator signs acceptance on arrival. We’ve attached the chain_of_custody_template.xlsx and a draft site-acceptance-form.pdf for review.
- Fingerprint verification: we will provide both SHA256 and a QR encoding of the fingerprint on the printed manifest; the QR decodes to the SHA256 and a drive link to the signed manifest (read-only).

Operational asks for NorthStar: please confirm preferred SFTP endpoint for the acceptance PDF and the PGP or SFTP public key we should use for secure uploads. If SFTP is not possible, scanned PDFs via email signed by the operator are acceptable but slower for audit.

Attachments referenced: [attachment: island_manifest_v1.2.tar.sig (detached signature)], [attachment: site-acceptance-form.pdf], [attachment: chain_of_custody_template.xlsx].

Connor / Marissa — please confirm we have HSM audit entry for the signing event and that the signer certificate will be attached to the bundle.

Mina
Mina Haddad
Lead, Deployment Security
Redwood Inference

On Fri, Sep 12, 2025 at 11:18 AM Carla Vega <carla.vega@aegis-svcs.com> wrote:

>
> Thanks for the summary. NorthStar ops confirms the week of Sep 22 is acceptable...
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Island deployment artifact signing & acceptance — proposed window

Thanks — a couple practical items from ops scheduling:

- Lab dry-run: recommend we run a single activation in our sealed lab (with Diego’s operator on the call if possible) the week prior to shipment (Sep 15–18). This validates that the operator can verify the signature and complete the acceptance form end-to-end.
- Emergency rollback: propose we escrow an encrypted rollback token with Aegis (sealed envelope) that NorthStar can use only after a two-person authorization (Redwood + NorthStar). Details to follow — need sign-off from Diego.
- Printing: we’ll include QR + human-readable fingerprint and a short verification URL on the printed manifest.

Carla — can Aegis facilitate a short remote session during the lab dry-run to coach the operator through the verification steps? That will cut acceptance time on-site.

Connor
Connor O'Brien
Deployment Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Island deployment artifact signing & acceptance — final signed manifest + next steps

Carla / Diego —

Thanks for confirming details. Attached is the final signed manifest (island_manifest_v1.2.tar.sig) and the one-page signing statement: it includes the certificate chain, HSM slot id (redwood-hsm-2), and UTC signing timestamp. We’ve also attached a pre-filled site-acceptance-form.pdf for Diego to review — please sign and return after acceptance.

Nearby next steps:
- Sep 18: Lab dry-run (09:00 PT) — remote session with Diego and Aegis to validate verification flow. Connor will send calendar invite.
- Sep 21 (end of day): Redwood delivers signed bundle to Aegis courier.
- Sep 22 (08:00–11:00 local): Aegis attempts delivery to NorthStar site; operator performs verification and returns signed site-acceptance-form.pdf to ops SFTP.

Escalation / rollback: we are preparing an encrypted rollback token (sealed envelope with Aegis) available at depot; to use it a two-party auth is required (Redwood ops + NorthStar security, documented by signed form).

Please confirm:
1) Diego — you can attend the Sep 18 dry-run at 09:00 PT?
2) Carla / Aegis — confirm courier pickup on Sep 21 and that the courier will co-sign the chain_of_custody_template.xlsx at dispatch.

If all good, we’ll finalize printed manifests and schedule the courier.

Thanks —
Karthik

--
